newsitem.title: MEXICO: Salomon hails Mexican cement price decision.
newsitem.headline: Salomon hails Mexican cement price decision.

text.p: Salomon Brothers on Tuesday hailed a decision by Mexican cement producers Cemex and Apasco to eliminate price discounts implemented in the fourth quarter of 1996 and reiterated its buy recommendations on both firms.
"This is good news, since the elimination of discounts occured sooner than expected," Salomon analyst Carmen Slade said in a report.
She said the price increases were expected to be in the order of 10-to-11 percent in nominal peso terms.

"What we are seeing is a recovery to, in Apasco's case, and a possible slight increase over, in Cemex's case, third quarter 1996 levels before pricing pressures took hold starting in October," she said.

After Cemex raised prices less than Apasco last July, Slade said Apasco dropped prices from about $79 per ton in Q3 to $73 per ton in Q4, and is expected to push them back up to around $78-79 this quarter.
She said Cemex's average realized prices, meanwhile, were $79 per ton in Q3, $74.5 per ton in November and December, and should be around $80 in Q1.
